rationale:
All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent but still aligned). Best-supported pick: PGS003972 is from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet; many AAA-relevant cohorts listed) using genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CS) with a large variant set, which is structurally favored for polygenic traits; it also reports a full-model AUROC=0.69 (not PRS-only) with EUR evaluation. Main limitation: reported discrimination is not PRS-only/comparable (no PGS-only AUROC/R2/OR per SD), and covariates are listed as Unknown, reducing comparability and confidence.

Runner-up 1 (PGS003973): same disease-focused Nat Genet study family and same method/variant count with EUR evaluation; reports a high full-model C-index=0.882, but this is likely covariate-driven (covariates include Age/Age^2/Sex) and is not PRS-only, so it is discounted per the provided domain guidance; otherwise it remains a strong direct-match sibling.

Runner-up 2 (PGS000753): exact AAA endpoint (prevalent AAA) and provides a PRS-comparable effect size (OR per SD=1.37, moderate) plus basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), but it is an older sparse P+T score with only 29 variants, which is structurally weaker than genome-wide shrinkage models when other evidence is similar.

Other direct-match candidates were ranked lower: PGS001784 and PGS002054 come from framework/portability-style papers (Cell Genom global biobank PRS; AJHG portability of 245 scores) and their reported PRS-comparable metrics (R2 ~0.014–0.0147 / partial-r 0.0144) are modest; PGS003429 is a screening cost-effectiveness context with unknown covariates and only full-model metrics, offering limited standalone PRS evidence. | Borda re-rank promoted PGS003972 from runner-up positions.

All four candidates are direct matches for the target concept via trait_efo/phenotyping (AUD/alcohol dependence measurement). PGS002738 is best supported because it is explicitly mapped to trait_efo="alcohol dependence" with phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder" and provides a relatively strong, directly interpretable discrimination signal (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a sizable EUR evaluation (n=7,900) and multi-cohort development (MVP, UKB). Runners-up: PGS000201 is closely aligned (DSM-5 AUD criteria count) and reports an incremental ΔR²=0.01192 with a larger variant count and adequate EUR evaluation (n=7,599), but its trait_efo is the less-specific "alcohol dependence measurement" and it lacks OR/HR-style discrimination. PGS002739 remains a direct AUD/alcohol dependence model and reports OR top 10% vs rest = 1.76 (1.32–2.34), but it is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean (AFR) and uses a gene-based PRS-CSx approach with much fewer features, making it less generally supported from the visible evidence for an unspecified target context. Overall confidence is moderate (not high) because no candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R² and covariates are unknown for PGS002738/PGS002739, limiting comparability and strength of inference.

All three candidates are direct matches (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis / near-synonymous labels). PGS004913 is best supported because its phenotyping_reported exactly matches the target concept (“Alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis”), it is disease-focused, uses only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), and reports PRS-comparable signal (R²=0.029) plus an OR top vs bottom deciles of 4.4. Runner-up PGS001777 is also disease-focused and directly alcohol-related, with a strong risk-gradient metric (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18) but is limited by very sparse variants (3), unknown covariates, and a small validation sample (n=1,390), making robustness harder to judge. PGS000704 ranks third despite large validation and a genome-wide model, because the only reported discrimination is a full-model C-index/AUROC (0.711) from a broader biomarker-focused UKB paper; per the domain guidance, full-model AUROC is not a substitute for PRS-only performance, and its modest per-SD HR (1.18) suggests weaker standalone PRS signal. Overall confidence is moderate because none of the candidates provides clean PRS-only AUROC and the reported metrics are not directly comparable across studies.

All 19 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=angina pectoris; phenotyping spans Angina / ICD10 I20 / PheCode 411.3). PGS005052 is best supported because it has strong endpoint fidelity (Angina pectoris PheCode 411.3), reports a relatively high full-model discrimination metric (C-index 0.7662) plus a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.491, 95% CI 1.42–1.57), and is from a multi-ancestry evaluation context (AFR/AMR/EUR), which is supportive for robustness. The two strongest runners-up are PGS005048 (highest C-index among listed models at 0.7669 and OR 1.487) and PGS005057 (C-index 0.7664 and OR 1.479). Outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL rather than DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY because key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) are missing for these top MVP-derived models, making cross-model comparability and PRS-only signal strength less certain; additionally, several near-clone high-performing alternatives are essentially indistinguishable on the visible evidence. | Borda re-rank promoted PGS005052 from runner-up positions.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (ankylosing spondylitis) by trait_efo/trait_reported, with generally coherent phenotyping_reported (except one time-to-event variant). For best_model_id, PGS001267 is preferred because it provides the cleanest PRS-comparable performance evidence in this list (explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.7265 and PGS-only R2=0.0988, plus full-model AUROC=0.7433 with only basic covariates) and has endpoint-fidelity consistent with the generic target (phenotyping_reported: Ankylosing spondylitis). The main limitation is that it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly versus disease-focused efforts, lowering confidence.

Runners-up: (1) PGS001268 is a near-clone from the same framework family with slightly higher reported AUROC/R2, but its phenotyping_reported is explicitly time-to-event (TTE ankylosing spondylitis), which domain guidance treats as a mild endpoint mismatch for a generic disease-risk target; thus it ranks behind PGS001267 despite similar/stronger metrics. (2) PGS002089 is a direct ankylosing spondylitis score with a methodologically strong genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2; 22,026 variants) and a higher reported partial correlation (0.0919) than the sibling penalized-regression portability score (PGS001876 partial-r=0.0797), but it lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2 and comes from a UKB portability framework context, making the performance evidence less directly comparable than for PGS001267/PGS001268.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (aortic stenosis) are present: PGS005252, PGS005254, PGS005255, and PGS005256 (the remaining models are for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and are not direct matches). PGS005252 is best supported because it is an exact trait/efo match (Aortic stenosis; incident aortic stenosis cases), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDPred2) with a large variant set (1,119,377), reports a strong per-SD effect size (HR=1.92), and provides a high full-model C-index (0.87) on a large EUR evaluation set (n=446,895); while full-model metrics are not PRS-only, the effect size supports meaningful PRS signal. Runner-up PGS005254 is also an exact aortic stenosis model with incident endpoint and EUR evaluation, but has weaker reported effect size (HR=1.64) and lacks any reported discrimination metric in the visible metadata. Between the two measurement-labeled scores, PGS005255 and PGS005256 have identical variant counts/method/endpoint description and very similar HRs (both 1.53), making them effectively indistinguishable; PGS005255 is selected as the second runner-up arbitrarily only because no differentiating evidence is visible. Main limitation lowering confidence: none of the aortic stenosis candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R², and PGS005252’s reported C-index is from a covariate-adjusted full model with multiple clinical risk factors, so comparability of discrimination across candidates is limited.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, including an exact EFO match: PGS001135 (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Arthritis (nos)” / “arthritis”). This provides the strongest phenotype alignment in the visible list. However, its evidence is limited by being a pan-trait UK Biobank framework score (“Significant sparse polygenic risk scores across 813 traits in UK Biobank”) with weak PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.539; PGS R2=0.00291) and very small incremental AUROC (0.00314), suggesting limited standalone PRS signal.

Runners-up were selected from the other direct arthritis EFO matches: PGS004477 and PGS004547 (both “M13 (Other arthritis)” with trait_efo=arthritis). These are also direct matches but have weaker/less comparable performance evidence in the provided metadata (only an OR is shown, no AUROC/R2; covariates are unknown), making them harder to prefer over PGS001135 despite the latter’s modest PRS-only metrics. Overall, the presence of direct matches supports selection, but the best option remains sub-optimal due to weak PRS-only signal and incomplete comparable metrics across the other direct-match candidates.

All listed candidates are direct matches to asthma (trait_efo=asthma), but they vary in endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable evidence. PGS002727 is explicitly disease-focused for the target population segment (phenotyping_reported: pediatric asthma) and provides strong PRS-discriminative evidence via a per-SD effect size (OR=1.57, 95% CI 1.55–1.60; meets the domain-knowledge ‘strong’ OR≥1.5 guideline) plus a reported full-model AUROC=0.66 and R²=0.04, with very large validation (n=391,820) and multi-ancestry evaluation. Main limitation: endpoint is pediatric-only (not generic asthma) and covariates are ‘Unknown’, lowering comparability and making it unclear how much reported AUROC reflects PRS vs covariates.

Runner-up 1 (PGS001782): direct asthma endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Asthma) with genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CS-auto; 884,043 variants) and reported covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R²=0.048844 plus full-model AUROC=0.659 in EUR evaluation. Limitation: comes from a ‘Global Biobank analyses…’ framework-style paper per domain knowledge, which is generally penalized versus disease-focused models when available.

Runner-up 2 (PGS001344): direct doctor-diagnosed asthma endpoint with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.64568; PGS-only R²=0.05973) and incremental AUROC=0.07977, but it is from the ‘across 813 traits in UK Biobank’ pan-trait framework family (snpnet), which domain knowledge flags as often underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation. The overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because multiple direct-match candidates have substantial but non-comparable evidence (different endpoints, covariate regimes, and several framework-origin scores), leaving meaningful uncertainty about the single best general-purpose asthma PRS.

All 6 candidates are direct EFO matches to atopic eczema, but they differ materially in endpoint fidelity and comparability. PGS002755 is the best-supported direct-match because its reported endpoint is incident atopic dermatitis (well-aligned to generic atopic eczema risk), it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,090,702 variants; structurally strong for a polygenic trait), and it reports a PRS-associated HR (high vs low PRS) with CI in a very large European evaluation (n=337,910). The main limitation is that no PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided, so effect-size evidence is limited to a single HR contrast and cross-model metric comparability is weak.

Runners-up: PGS004587 also targets incident atopic dermatitis and reports a similar HR with CI in the same large European evaluation size, but it is a sparse genome-wide-significant SNP score (23 variants), which is structurally weaker than PRS-CS for a polygenic disease and offers no clearer performance advantage. PGS001773 is a direct atopic dermatitis score but is restricted to moderate-to-severe disease in Canadian cohorts and reports only full-model AUROC/R2 (0.93/0.49) with demographic/ethnicity covariates; per domain guidance, full-model AUROC is not a substitute for PRS-only performance and the very high values raise concern that discrimination is largely covariate-driven and/or not comparable. The remaining candidates (PGS003459, PGS003486, PGS004903) are therapy-specific ‘paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis’ endpoints, which are poorer matches to generic atopic eczema risk despite being eczema-labeled.

All highlighted candidates are direct matches to atrial fibrillation by trait_reported/trait_efo, so ranking is driven by endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported), PRS-comparable evidence, and study archetype/covariate cleanliness per the provided domain_knowledge. PGS005168 is best supported because it is a disease-focused AF meta-analysis PRS (Nat Genet; multi-cohort training_development_cohorts list) with a direct AF endpoint (phenotyping_reported: atrial fibrillation), basic-plus-clinical-risk adjustment that is explicitly flagged as not heavy leakage in the guidance (age/age^2/sex/PCs/array plus CHARGE-AF), and strong reported discrimination (C-index 0.8718 with CI) alongside a strong per-SD effect size signal (HR 1.6663). Key limitation: the reported C-index appears to be a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only), and inclusion of CHARGE-AF means the very high C-index cannot be interpreted as PRS-only performance, lowering certainty to Moderate. Runner-up PGS005313 is also a disease-focused, multi-cohort AF score with strong effect size (OR 1.82 with tight CI) and reported AUROC 0.78 with only basic covariates (age, sex), but it is evaluated in a non-EUR-only setting (EVAL: MAE 100%) and has less extensive visible validation detail than PGS005168. Third, PGS000331 (Nat Med) remains a strong older disease-focused multi-cohort incident AF model with basic covariates and supportive effect size (HR 1.62) and C-index 0.751, but it is less compelling than the two newer multi-cohort AF-specific models given the weaker reported discrimination and no PRS-only metrics.

Direct-match candidates are present (4 total). PGS001263 is the most endpoint-faithful to the target, with trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all explicitly 'Atrial flutter'. It also reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.61716; PGS R2 no covariates=0.02517) and these are plausible under the provided heritability ceiling guidance (h2_obs=0.0157; h2_liability=0.1443), supporting interpretability. Main limitation: it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework ("across 813 traits"; snpnet/L1-sparse style), which domain guidance flags as often less externally robust than disease-focused development; additionally, the higher full-model AUROC is likely covariate-influenced and should not be treated as PRS-only evidence.

Runner-up 1 (PGS001339) remains well-supported because it directly includes atrial flutter in the combined AF/flutter endpoint and reports similar PRS-only metrics, but it is less specific (AF+flutter) and uses a time-to-event phenotype, which domain guidance treats as a mild endpoint penalty for a generic disease target.

Runner-up 2 (PGS002050) is also a direct concept match (AF+flutter) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very high variant count, but it lacks PRS-comparable AUROC/R2 (only partial-r is provided), reducing comparability versus the snpnet models; it is also from a portability framework paper, which is not a clear advantage absent stronger endpoint/metric evidence. (PGS001841 is similar to PGS002050 but with slightly lower partial-r and fewer variants, so it ranks below.)

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to autism spectrum disorder). PGS000327 is best supported because its endpoint fidelity is coherent across fields (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all explicitly “Autism spectrum disorder”), it comes from a disease-focused ASD GWAS publication (“Identification of common genetic risk variants for autism spectrum disorder.”, Nat Genet), and it reports supportive PRS-relevant evidence including an OR per SD of 1.33 (moderate) and an R² metric (0.0245) in European validation with basic covariates (genetic PCs, genotyping wave). PGS002790 is a weaker runner-up because its phenotyping_reported is explicitly mismatched/withdrawn (“Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)”) despite the ASD trait label, and its reported partial R² (0.00546) is materially smaller; additionally, training sample size is N/A, further limiting interpretability. Confidence is Moderate (not High) because neither model reports clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics (e.g., PGS-only AUC/R²), and PGS000327’s reported R² appears to be a full-model metric rather than explicitly PRS-only, which limits cross-model comparability.

All 20 listed candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_efo = basal cell carcinoma). For best-model selection, endpoint fidelity and comparable performance evidence dominate. PGS000452 has a clean, direct endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Basal cell carcinoma) with only basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), EUR development/evaluation, and is among the strongest on the visible validation metrics in this list (full-model AUROC 0.632; Nagelkerke R² 0.0487; per-SD OR 1.663; top-1% vs rest OR 3.61). Two close runners-up from the same coherent Cancer PRSweb family are PGS000454 (same endpoint/covariates/ancestry; full-model AUROC 0.632; Nagelkerke R² 0.0489; per-SD OR 1.661; top-1% vs rest OR 3.79) and PGS000456 (same endpoint/covariates/ancestry; full-model AUROC 0.63; Nagelkerke R² 0.0456; per-SD OR 1.633; top-1% vs rest OR 3.95). Confidence is Moderate because none of the candidates report PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R², so rankings rely on full-model metrics and effect sizes; additionally, several near-clone PRSweb models are extremely close on reported performance, making fine ordering somewhat unstable from the visible metadata alone.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target concept (trait_efo includes/equals “bilirubin metabolism disease”). PGS002032 is preferred because it has the most endpoint-faithful and specific phenotype among the set (“Disorders of bilirubin excretion” in both trait_reported and phenotyping_reported) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with a large variant set (19,768), which is a positive structural signal for polygenic traits when comparable PRS-only metrics are not available. Main limitation: both PGS002032 and its sibling PGS001824 lack PRS-comparable AUC/R² in the visible metadata (only partial-r is reported), so the choice relies heavily on method/structure rather than directly comparable discrimination metrics. Runner-up PGS001824 is the same endpoint from the same publication but uses penalized regression with far fewer variants (22) and no stronger performance evidence than PGS002032 (same partial-r). PGS000924 is ranked third despite reporting high apparent AUROC/R² because it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”), has a time-to-event composite endpoint (“Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism (time-to-event)”) rather than the specific bilirubin-excretion disorder, and its very high full-model AUROC is not a substitute for missing PRS-only comparability per the provided domain guidance.

All three candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo to the bipolar disorder spectrum (bipolar disorder, bipolar I, bipolar II). However, endpoint fidelity is weak/unclear across all three because phenotyping_reported fields are non-diagnostic proxy/adjacent measures (cognitive/behavioral phenotypes) rather than a bipolar disorder case-control/diagnosis endpoint, which the domain guidance prioritizes. No PRS-comparable AUC/R2 is provided; the only visible metric is a small partial R² from a European validation, and covariates are basic (age, PCs1-3) across all models, making performance evidence limited and largely indistinguishable. Given otherwise near-clone metadata (same method SDPR, same publication/date, EUR-only GWAS/EVAL, PGC training cohort), PGS002786 is selected as the best direct-match mainly on the broadest concept alignment to the target trait (bipolar disorder rather than subtype) and slightly higher variant count, but this is a weak differentiator; runners-up are ranked by the available partial R² (PGS002788 > PGS002787) with the caveat that these differences are small and not clearly PRS-only.

All three visible candidates are direct matches at the broad level (all map to the coagulation-disease space), but none is strongly supported because two lack standard PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (AUC/R²) and the remaining one is a pan-trait sparse UKB framework score with an extremely low variant count.

Best (PGS002034): Chosen because its phenotype/trait is a specific coagulation disorder endpoint (“Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)”) and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with a large variant set (32,552), a structural positive signal when performance metrics are otherwise limited. It also reports a partial correlation (partial-r 0.0563, EUR validation) providing at least some comparable performance evidence.

Runner-up 1 (PGS001826): Same endpoint, same publication family, similar partial-r (0.0562) and validation context; ranked below PGS002034 primarily due to much smaller variant count (45) and a less structurally strong method choice relative to LDpred2, with no other differentiating evidence visible.

Runner-up 2 (PGS001033): Has explicit AUROC/PRS-only AUROC fields available, but the score is from a pan-trait “813 traits in UK Biobank” sparse framework (snpnet) and is effectively non-polygenic here (variants_number=1) with a time-to-event phenotype label, both warning signals for external reliability; therefore it is deprioritized despite having more complete AUC reporting.

Main limitation: the top two candidates (PGS002034/PGS001826) provide only partial-correlation metrics (no AUC/R²), and all candidates are UKB-derived framework/portability contexts rather than clearly disease-focused multi-cohort coagulation studies, keeping confidence below high.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo=breast carcinoma and phenotyping_reported as breast cancer/incident breast cancer). Among the visible set, PGS004153 is best supported because it is a direct breast cancer model with no added covariates (covariates=0) and reports the strongest discrimination/variance metrics in the same coherent evaluation family (Am J Hum Genet 2023-12-19 multi-method benchmarking in UKB; full_model_auc=0.6625 and R²=0.0764, with strong OR per SD ~1.83). The two closest runners-up from the same high-support cluster are PGS004040 and PGS004025, which share the same endpoint/covariate context and have nearly identical but slightly lower reported AUROC/R² and effect sizes. Limitation: the selected metrics are full-model (not explicitly PGS-only), and several other direct-match candidates exist with different study designs/covariates (e.g., family-history/clinical-risk-model–augmented models or pan-trait frameworks), making cross-study comparability imperfect; thus confidence is Moderate rather than High.

All 10 visible candidates are direct matches to celiac disease by trait_efo, but they vary in endpoint specificity and metric comparability. PGS000316 is best supported because it targets an uncomplicated coeliac disease endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Coeliac disease), is disease-focused (clinical-care pilot study), and reports strong discrimination (full-model AUROC=0.879 with tight CI) with very large validation (n=379,767), providing unusually robust evidence among the direct-match set. Main limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R²), and covariates are listed as Unknown, so the PRS-only contribution cannot be isolated.

Runner-up PGS000040 is also disease-focused with a direct coeliac disease endpoint and reports very high AUROC=0.90, but its evidence is weaker due to smaller validation (n=2,476) and similarly lacking PRS-only metrics/covariate clarity. Runner-up PGS001301 has explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.8287; PGS R²=0.1422) and standard demographic/PC covariates, but it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper and uses a broader phenotype label (“Malabsorption/coeliac disease”), which domain guidance treats as less reliable than disease-focused models when such models exist. Other candidates are either restricted to HLA-DQ2.5 carriers (PGS000041/PGS000042) or are portability-framework scores with only partial-correlation metrics (PGS001856/PGS001894/PGS002067/PGS002107) or show weaker AUROC (PGS004930).

All 6 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). PGS003428 is best supported on structural grounds: it is a disease-focused cervical-phenotype GWAS meta-analysis study (“GWAS meta-analyses clarify genetics of cervical phenotypes…”) using a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with very large variant count (2,894,555), and it reports a moderate per-SD effect size (HR=1.33) with incident cervical cancer and relatively light covariates (age, smoking). Main limitation: only a full-model C-index is reported (0.613) with no PGS-only metrics, and the training sample size shown (n=4,295) is small/unclear relative to typical GWAS meta-analyses, lowering certainty.

Runners-up: PGS000073 and PGS000784 are near-clone, endpoint-faithful incident cervical cancer scores from related Nat Commun cross-/pan-cancer risk prediction papers, with large European evaluation (n=211,795) and similar full-model discrimination (AUROC≈0.745) plus moderate HR per SD (~1.21–1.22). They are ranked below PGS003428 because they are GWAS-hits (10 variants) rather than genome-wide shrinkage, and their high AUROC is full-model (covariate-boosted) rather than PRS-only. PGS000073 is placed slightly above PGS000784 because PGS000784 explicitly uses inverse variant weights from PGS000073, offering no clear improvement signal beyond being a reparameterization.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis (some via ICD10 K80; two via a composite endpoint including cholecystitis). The strongest visible support cluster is the matched sibling pair from the same publication (“Portability of 245 polygenic scores…”, UKB-derived) because they share a coherent endpoint (“Cholelithiasis and cholecystitis”), basic covariates, and provide PRS-comparable effect evidence (partial correlation with CI). Between these siblings, PGS002072 is mildly preferred over PGS001861 due to slightly higher reported partial-r (0.098 vs 0.0948) and a more methodologically strong genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) relative to penalized regression in this context. Runners-up: PGS001861 remains the closest competitor as the near-identical sibling model with only a small metric gap. PGS001174 is ranked next because it reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.623; PGS-only R2 0.028) with basic covariates and its PRS-only R2 remains below the provided EUR heritability ceiling (h2_obs 0.0214; liability 0.1372), but it is from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as a generalization risk. The K80 models (PGS004476/PGS004546) and the EAS-evaluated PRS-CSx model (PGS005150) are penalized here because they lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and provide only modest effect sizes (OR ~1.22–1.30; β reported without clear scale), making them harder to justify over candidates with clearer PRS-comparable evidence. Overall confidence is moderate because the top candidates lack AUROC/R2 and rely on partial-r (whose comparability to AUROC/R2 is limited), and the best-vs-runner-up differences are small.

All listed candidates are direct EFO matches to chronic kidney disease, so ranking hinges on endpoint fidelity plus PRS-informative performance evidence and study archetype. PGS002237 is best supported because it is explicitly CKD stage 3+ (eGFR <45) with a disease-focused publication (“Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries.”, Nat Med), multi-ancestry evaluation, and reports strong full-model AUROC (0.78) alongside a moderate per-SD effect size (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.32–1.65), consistent with meaningful PRS contribution. Runner-up PGS005090 is also endpoint-faithful (CKD stage 3+; phenotyping_reported CKD) and reports very strong discrimination (AUROC 0.9; R2 0.1; OR 1.41) in an African-American evaluation context, but its single-ancestry (AFR-only) setting makes it less universally supported from the visible evidence. Second runner-up PGS004158 is an endpoint-faithful CKD score with the strongest full-model AUROC among the five-biobank method-benchmark siblings (AUROC ~0.592; R2 ~0.020) and uses no covariates (clean comparability), but these benchmark-family scores show substantially weaker discrimination than PGS002237 and are evaluated only in EUR/SAS. Confidence is Moderate because many candidates lack PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2), several report only full-model AUROC or effect sizes, and some candidates have endpoint/covariate packaging that reduces comparability (e.g., incident-only, exposure-interaction, or heavy clinical covariates), limiting decisive separation beyond the top choice.

Direct-match COPD candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo = chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and phenotyping_reported explicitly COPD/J44/chronic airway obstruction). Among these, PGS001783 is best supported by the visible evidence because it is endpoint-aligned (phenotyping_reported: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto; 884,139 variants), comes from a broad multi-biobank development context, and reports a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.038092) plus an AUROC value (0.74, noting this is not explicitly PGS-only). The top runners-up are PGS001788 (same study family/method/endpoint but weaker reported covariates-regressed-out R2 = 0.0163) and PGS001332 (exact COPD label/phenotype but from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework with low PGS-only AUROC ~0.54 and very small PGS-only R2 ~0.00235, despite having explicit PGS-only metrics). Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL rather than high quality because key performance fields are not fully comparable across candidates (e.g., AUROC sometimes appears to be full-model; many models lack explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2), and several direct matches come from framework/portability papers or have limited metric reporting, leaving residual uncertainty in ranking.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to the target disease concept (cirrhosis of liver) via either exact cirrhosis (trait_efo=cirrhosis of liver) or a clearly labeled etiologic subtype (alcoholic/alcohol-associated cirrhosis). PGS004621 is best supported overall because it has the cleanest phenotype alignment (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both “Cirrhosis”), a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (1,089,806), and large-scale multi-cohort development/validation context (multiple biobanks listed; validation_sample_size n=1,153,995). Its reported metric is a full-model AUROC=0.68 with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), which is at least comparable across candidates that also mainly report full-model metrics. Main limitation: no PRS-only (covariate-free) AUC/R2 is provided for any candidate here, so discrimination comparisons are inherently uncertain and full-model AUROC is not a substitute for PRS-only performance.

The two strongest runners-up are PGS000076 and its closely related sibling PGS000787: both are endpoint-faithful (incident kidney cancer) with similar covariates and report full-model AUROC ~0.722 plus HR ~1.15–1.16, but they show weaker effect size evidence than PGS004908 and (per domain guidance) their full-model AUROC is not a PRS-only metric, limiting comparability. Confidence is Moderate because most candidates lack PRS-only (covariate-free) AUC/R², making cross-model performance comparisons partially non-comparable, and because PGS000787’s reported R²=0.366 is difficult to interpret as PRS-comparable given the domain heritability ceiling note for kidney cancer and the lack of explicit PRS-only metric labeling in the visible metadata.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (kidney failure) are present, including PGS004562 (N18 Chronic renal failure; trait_efo=kidney failure), PGS004492 (N18 Chronic renal failure; trait_efo=kidney failure), and PGS000708 (trait_reported=Kidney failure; trait_efo=kidney failure). PGS004562 is best supported on visible evidence because it is an exact trait_efo match to kidney failure and shows the strongest reported per-SD effect size among the kidney-failure–labeled models (OR=1.39548), which domain guidance treats as a meaningful PRS-quality signal when AUC/R2 are absent. PGS004492 is the closest runner-up with the same endpoint coding (N18 chronic renal failure; trait_efo=kidney failure) but weaker effect size (OR=1.1708). PGS000708 is a reasonable third choice due to exact kidney-failure labeling and reported C-index/full-model discrimination (0.779) plus HR=1.19, but its phenotyping is explicitly restricted to diabetic kidney failure and the reported discrimination is full-model (not PRS-only), limiting comparability. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because the leading kidney-failure candidates (PGS004562/PGS004492) lack PRS-comparable performance metrics and have unknown covariates, leaving residual uncertainty despite strong endpoint alignment.

All 7 candidates are direct matches via trait_efo=osteoarthritis, knee (or a knee OA arthroplasty endpoint for PGS002749). PGS002767 is best supported because it has exact endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: knee osteoarthritis), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,052,275 variants), and reports a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.35, 95% CI 1.3–1.4) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, technical). The main limitation is that it lacks PRS-comparable metrics (no PGS-only AUC/R²), so comparative ranking relies on structural signals and effect size rather than directly comparable discrimination.

Runner-up PGS002729 is also an exact knee osteoarthritis model with a disease-focused publication and multi-cohort development context; however, the only visible discrimination is a full-model AUROC=0.66 with covariates including BMI (and no PGS-only metrics), making it less comparable for PRS-only quality than an explicit per-SD OR from a genome-wide PRS. Runner-up PGS004549 is endpoint-aligned (gonarthrosis of knee) and uses an explicit multi-score aggregation method (RFDiseasemetaPRS), with a similar moderate effect size (OR=1.366693) and large variant count, but has unknown covariates and no comparable PRS-only metrics, lowering confidence relative to PGS002767.

Other candidates are less preferred on visible evidence: PGS001192 is from a pan-trait UKB framework ("across 813 traits") with time-to-event phenotyping and modest PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.56; R² 0.0068), which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused alternatives; PGS004479 is a sibling of PGS004549 with slightly weaker OR; PGS004883 is incident-only and appears to be a risk/incidence framework with small training n (404) and only full-model C-index; PGS002749 targets total knee replacement (advanced OA proxy), not generic knee OA.

All five listed candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_efo = late-onset Alzheimer's disease), but the pool has limited PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (no PGS-only AUROC/R² reported; most AUC fields are null), so selection relies mainly on endpoint fidelity plus effect-size evidence and structural plausibility.

PGS000054 is preferred because it is endpoint-faithful (familial late-onset AD), uses basic covariates (age, sex), and provides the strongest visible per-SD effect size signal (OR=1.73, 95% CI 1.57–1.93) among candidates—domain guidance treats OR≥1.5 as strong discriminative evidence when AUROC/R² are absent. It is also part of a coherent disease-focused publication family (same Neurology paper as PGS000053) with similar construction (21 GWAS-significant variants), reducing concerns about idiosyncratic design.

Runner-up PGS000053 is essentially the same disease-focused sibling score with the same endpoint framing and covariates, but shows a weaker effect size (OR=1.29, 1.21–1.37), providing less direct support for discriminative power.

Second runner-up PGS000334 has clean endpoint labeling for late-onset AD and a more polygenic construction than the GWAS-hits scores (C+T; 22 variants), but its only reported metric is an R²=0.191 labeled as “proportion of variance explained” (not explicitly PRS-only) with unknown covariates; domain guidance flags unusually high R² from simple thresholding with unclear covariates as potentially non-comparable/inflated, so it cannot be confidently promoted over the effect-size-supported Neurology scores.

PGS002289 is deprioritized despite very large validation n because its phenotyping_reported is a cognition×age interaction outcome rather than AD diagnosis, weakening endpoint fidelity for a LOAD PRS. PGS004918 reports only a full-model AUROC (0.731) on a very small evaluation (n=136) with unknown covariates, and domain guidance cautions against treating full-model AUROC as PRS-only evidence.

Overall confidence is Moderate (not High) because the candidate set lacks clearly comparable PRS-only performance metrics and several records have endpoint/covariate ambiguity. | Borda re-rank promoted PGS000054 from runner-up positions.

All ranked candidates are direct matches to the target trait (lung cancer / lung carcinoma) by trait_reported/trait_efo and have diagnosis-anchored phenotyping_reported (incident lung cancer or lung cancer). PGS000078 is best supported overall because it targets incident lung cancer, is evaluated in EUR, has very large validation (n=392,539), and reports consistent effect size (HR=1.16) alongside strong reported discrimination metrics (AUROC=0.846; C-index=0.849). However, confidence is not High because the visible AUROC/C-index appear to be full-model metrics with substantial covariate adjustment (including family history, PM2.5, and detailed smoking interaction terms), and no PRS-only (no-covariates) AUROC/R2 is provided, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates.

Runners-up: PGS000789 is essentially the same endpoint/covariate/validation context and performance as PGS000078 (explicitly derived from it with inverse weights), making it a very strong alternative but not clearly superior from the provided metadata. PGS004860 is a newer LDpred2 genome-wide score with very high reported AUROC (0.893) and an OR=1.33, but it is also reported as a full model with covariates and has a much smaller validation sample (n=24,012); without PRS-only metrics, its apparent advantage could be covariate-driven and is not decisively stronger than the large, coherent PGS000078/PGS000789 evidence cluster. | Borda re-rank promoted PGS000078 from runner-up positions.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target concept (lupus erythematosus), mostly via systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) endpoints; however, comparably interpretable PRS-only metrics are largely absent and many reported AUROCs appear to be full-model rather than PRS-only, limiting certainty.

Best pick: PGS000328 is a direct SLE model with a clear diagnosis-aligned phenotype (SLE, early onset) and the strongest reported discrimination in the visible pool among the more straightforward SLE risk-score candidates (full-model AUROC=0.83 in EUR; n=1,001). While the phenotype is somewhat restricted (onset before age 20), it remains within the target disease entity and avoids explicit non-genetic “phenotype risk score” packaging.

Runners-up: (1) PGS000754 has a clean SLE endpoint and a genome-wide shrinkage method (lassosum) with very large variant count (293,684), which is structurally favorable for polygenic signal capture; its reported full-model AUROC is lower (0.65), but AUROC comparability is limited anyway. (2) PGS004917 is a direct SLE endpoint with supportive effect-size evidence (OR=2.01 reported) and moderate full-model AUROC (0.696), but it is tied to an interaction-focused study context (smoking interactions) and evaluated in a Middle Eastern ancestry cohort only (MAE), which makes general direct-match deployment less clearly supported from the visible metadata.

Key limitation driving DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL: the pool lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2 and incremental metrics for most candidates, and one high-AUROC candidate (PGS003960; AUROC=0.89) is explicitly adjusted with a “phenotype risk score” covariate (severe comparability leakage per provided domain guidance), preventing confident selection based on headline AUROC. | Borda re-rank promoted PGS000328 from runner-up positions.

Direct-match candidates are present (13 total) spanning lymphoid leukemia broadly and chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) subtypes. PGS000788 is the best-supported direct match because it targets incident lymphocytic leukemia (aligned to the target concept), is evaluated in a very large European cohort (n=391,338), and shows the strongest per-SD effect size signal among the broadly lymphoid-leukemia–aligned models (HR=1.7) with consistent time-to-event discrimination (AUROC 0.738; C-index 0.756) under basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs). Runners-up: PGS000077 is a near-identical endpoint match (incident lymphocytic leukemia) from the same study family with the same large evaluation cohort but weaker effect size/metrics (HR=1.45; AUROC 0.719; C-index 0.735). PGS000874 is a strong CLL-specific score with high reported C-index (0.861) and strong OR (3.79), but its phenotyping is explicitly restricted (CLL in individuals with family history of hematological cancers), which is a comparability concern for the generic target trait and likely inflates/limits generalizability. Overall limitation: across candidates, reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics (no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2), and several models are subtype- or cohort-restricted (CLL-only, family-history-enriched, or small validation n), so the best choice is supported but not definitive.

All 7 listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (macular degeneration / age-related macular degeneration), with strongest endpoint fidelity for those whose phenotyping_reported is explicit AMD diagnosis. PGS004606 is best supported because it is disease-focused (Nat Genet AMD across ancestries), has direct AMD phenotyping_reported, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; ~1.0M variants), and reports a full-model AUROC=0.71 with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), plus a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.76, 95% CI 1.73–1.78), which is supportive of meaningful PRS discrimination. Runners-up: PGS004607 is from the same strong disease-focused publication family and endpoint but shows weaker reported performance/effect size (AUROC=0.65; OR=1.48). PGS001013 is a direct macular degeneration model but is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused models; it does, however, provide explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC~0.553; PGS-only R2~0.006) that are heritability-plausible and thus keep it as the best-supported framework-type alternative. Main limitation lowering confidence: several other direct-match candidates (notably PGS004952 with an apparently very high AUROC but unclear metric scaling/interpretation and small validation n=1,232, and UKB portability scores PGS001834/PGS002041 with only modest partial-r) create uncertainty because PRS-comparable (PGS-only) discrimination metrics are largely missing for the disease-focused Nat Genet models, making cross-model performance comparisons imperfect.

Direct-match melanoma PRS candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo=melanoma / phenotyping_reported melanoma or incident invasive melanoma). Among the visible candidates, PGS002247 is best supported because it has high endpoint fidelity (incident invasive melanoma), reports comparatively strong discrimination (full_model AUROC=0.691; R²=0.072) in European validation, and comes from a melanoma-focused independent evaluation study (Br J Dermatol), reducing concern that the score is primarily a pan-trait/framework artifact. The two strongest runners-up from the same list are PGS002246 (same study, same endpoint, very similar performance: AUROC=0.688; R²=0.07) and PGS000743 (melanoma endpoint with higher reported full_model AUROC=0.74, but much smaller validation n=1,035 and no PRS-only metrics, making the apparent AUROC advantage less secure/comparable). Confidence is Moderate because many direct-match models exist with heterogeneous covariate sets and mostly full-model metrics (often without PRS-only AUROC/R²), which limits definitive cross-study comparability even though PGS002247 is a coherent, well-supported choice within the provided evidence.

All six visible candidates are nominally direct-match on concept (trait_reported is “Multiple myeloma” and trait_efo maps to plasma cell myeloma), but endpoint fidelity differs: PGS003450 is internally inconsistent because phenotyping_reported is “Chronic lymphocytic leukemia,” which is not multiple myeloma, so it is deprioritized despite sharing the trait labels. Among the remaining endpoint-aligned models, PGS002281 has the strongest visible discrimination evidence (full-model AUROC 0.644 with tight CI; OR 3.18 highest vs lowest quintiles) with clean/basic covariates (age, sex, geographic region) and EUR evaluation, making it the best-supported direct-match choice from the provided metadata. Runners-up: PGS002306 reports the highest full-model AUROC (0.69) but has a much smaller validation sample (n=290) and unknown covariates, reducing comparability; PGS000653 (Cancer PRSweb) is endpoint-aligned with basic covariates and larger validation (n=2,738) but shows lower full-model AUROC (0.577) and moderate per-SD OR (1.327). Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because none of the candidates report PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R², so comparisons rely on full-model metrics and effect sizes with limited cross-study comparability, lowering certainty.

All 7 visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (multiple sclerosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo, and most have phenotype-aligned endpoints (phenotyping_reported includes “Multiple sclerosis”). PGS000809 is best supported overall because it comes from a disease-focused MS study (not a pan-trait/portability framework), uses a multi-cohort MS context (many MS GWAS/consortium-style cohorts listed), has basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), and provides some quantitative validation evidence (full-model AUROC 0.765 and an R²=0.069 plus a reported β=0.63) in a European evaluation. The main limitation is that the reported AUROC appears to be full-model (not explicitly PGS-only), and comparably clean PRS-only metrics are missing for most non-framework candidates, making cross-model performance comparison uncertain.

Runners-up: PGS002726 is disease-focused and phenotype-aligned with the highest reported full-model AUROC (0.80) and a strong OR contrast (top 10% vs median OR=15), but it has small validation size (n=938) and unknown covariates, reducing comparability. PGS002038 is a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with supportive partial-r (0.0396) in a European-selected validation and is structurally strong versus sparse scores, but it comes from a UKB portability framework paper and lacks PRS-only AUROC/R², so its real-world external performance is uncertain. Pan-trait snpnet models (PGS001270/PGS001271) have explicit PGS-only metrics but are framework-derived and are therefore discounted relative to disease-focused candidates per the provided domain guidance.

Direct-match candidates for myocardial infarction are present (multiple models with trait_efo/phenotyping_reported indicating myocardial infarction or acute myocardial infarction). PGS005039 is selected as best supported because it is an exact MI endpoint (PheCode 411.2; phenotyping_reported: Myocardial infarction) with explicit validation discrimination (C-index 0.784836989151752) and a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.578, 95% CI 1.50–1.67), which is the strongest effect-size signal among the visible MI-labeled candidates and is prioritized by the provided domain-knowledge guidance over full-model AUROC alone. The two best-supported runners-up are PGS005035 (same MI endpoint family; similarly high C-index 0.783355... and strong OR 1.541, 95% CI 1.46–1.63) and PGS005045 (same endpoint family; C-index 0.783850... and OR 1.554, 95% CI 1.47–1.64). Main limitation: many top MI candidates come from the same 2024 HGG Adv comparison study and share similar design/metrics, making them nearly indistinguishable from the visible metadata; additionally, these are not PRS-only metrics (C-index is not explicitly labeled as PGS-only), so relative ranking relies heavily on effect-size magnitude and endpoint alignment rather than clean PRS-only R²/AUROC evidence.

Both visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = Nasal Cavity Polyp; phenotyping_reported = ICD10 J33 Nasal polyp) and come from the same publication, with identical EUR-only development/evaluation context (UKB; DEV/EVAL EUR 100%), same training (n=174,489) and validation sample size (n=56,192), and both lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 (only OR per SD reported; covariates unknown). With endpoint fidelity and study context effectively tied, the main differentiator is effect-size magnitude: PGS004535 reports a stronger OR (1.600668) than PGS004465 (1.3496), which the provided domain guidance treats as stronger evidence of PRS discriminative power when AUC/R2 are absent. Confidence is Moderate (not High) because covariates are unknown for both models and there are no PRS-only AUC/R2 metrics to corroborate the OR-based ranking; additionally, only two near-clone candidates are available, limiting cross-validation of the choice.

Direct-match candidates present (2/2) with consistent endpoint alignment: both PGS001830 and PGS002037 map to the target via trait_efo="nicotine dependence" and report/phenotype "Tobacco use disorder". Both are from the same UKB portability publication with identical training cohort (UKB), training N=391,124, similar covariates (basic demographics + PCs + deprivation), and the same validation sample size (n=19,400), so study-context signals do not differentiate them strongly. The main differentiator in visible evidence is the selected validation metric: PGS002037 shows higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0741, CI 0.0601–0.0881) than PGS001830 (0.0557, CI 0.0416–0.0697) in European validation, supporting PGS002037 as the better-performing direct match. Limitation: neither model reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2 (only partial-r is shown), and both originate from a portability/framework-style paper, so while one is preferred, overall certainty remains moderate rather than high.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (nodular goiter) via either nontoxic multinodular goiter (PGS001814, PGS002022) or benign nodular goiter (PGS005261–PGS005263), while two models (PGS005273, PGS005274) are case-control contrasts that include benign nodular goiter but are primarily framed as thyroid carcinoma vs benign nodular goiter (less endpoint-faithful for pure nodular goiter risk).

PGS005262 is best supported because it is explicitly aligned to benign nodular goiter (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all point to the target disease entity) and, among the benign nodular goiter models, it has the strongest visible performance evidence (highest full-model AUROC: 0.5933) plus a relatively strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.408), and uses a genome-wide continuous shrinkage method (PRSCS) with very high variant count (~1.09M), a positive structural signal when endpoints are aligned.

Runners-up: PGS005263 is the closest sibling (same endpoint and method family, similar variant count) with slightly weaker AUROC (0.5876) and OR (1.362). PGS005261 remains endpoint-aligned but is structurally weaker (P+T, 110 variants) and shows weaker effect size (OR 1.048) despite a comparable AUROC (0.5854), making it a less supported choice than the PRSCS siblings.

Main limitation: for PGS005261–PGS005263 only full-model AUROC is reported and covariates are listed as Unknown, so the AUROC comparability and the standalone PRS contribution cannot be verified from the provided metadata; this keeps confidence at Moderate despite clear endpoint alignment and consistent sibling evidence.

All 10 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (obesity) by trait_efo and/or phenotyping_reported, so this is a direct-match selection problem with multiple plausible options. PGS002033 is preferred because it has strong phenotype alignment ("Overweight, obesity and other hyperalimentation"), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very high variant count (846,292), and reports the strongest available PRS-comparable performance signal in this list (partial correlation 0.0789, higher than PGS001825’s 0.0547). Runners-up: PGS001825 is the closest sibling from the same publication family (same endpoint and covariates) but with weaker partial-r and a smaller model signal; PGS005235 is also endpoint-faithful (phenotyping_reported: obesity phecode 278.1) and uses LDpred2-auto with a high variant count, but lacks PRS-comparable metrics in the provided metadata (only an OR is shown without clarity on scale), lowering certainty. Overall confidence is moderate (not high) because most candidates lack directly comparable PRS-only AUC/R², several come from framework/portability contexts (which are penalized by the provided domain guidance), and the available effect-size/metric reporting is heterogeneous across studies, limiting a decisive, high-certainty ranking.

All 13 listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo, with several also having phenotype-aligned endpoints (e.g., Osteoporosis; M81 osteoporosis without pathological fracture). The strongest PRS-comparable evidence in the visible set comes from effect sizes: PGS005155 (PRS-CSx; EAS evaluation) reports the largest per-SD effect (β=1.1443) among the effect-size-only models and uses a cross-ancestry GWAS (EAS+EUR) with EAS-only evaluation, making it the best-supported direct-match for East Asian deployment specifically. Runner-up PGS005146 (PRS-CS; EAS GWAS/EAS eval) is slightly weaker by effect size (β=1.0937) but remains endpoint-aligned and ancestry-consistent. For a European-validated alternative with explicit PRS-only metrics, PGS001274 (snpnet; TTE osteoporosis without pathological fracture) and PGS001273 (snpnet; osteoporosis) report PGS-only AUROC/R2, but they come from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused scores; additionally, their very high full-model AUROC appears largely covariate-driven (small incremental AUROC and small PGS-only R2), limiting confidence. Among the EUR-only modern-method options, PGS004810 (PRSmixPlus; incremental R2=0.022) provides the clearest PRS contribution signal within its study, exceeding PGS004809 (incremental R2=0.011), but it is still limited by modest validation size and lack of PRS-only AUROC/R2. Overall confidence is Moderate because the best choice depends on intended ancestry (EAS vs EUR) and much of the candidate set lacks directly comparable PRS-only discrimination metrics. | Borda re-rank promoted PGS005155 from runner-up positions.

Both visible candidates are direct matches to otosclerosis (trait_efo=otosclerosis). PGS002046 is preferred on structural grounds: it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with a much larger variant set (570,308) and has a PRS-comparable reported metric (partial correlation partial-r=0.0182 with CI), whereas PGS001255 is a very sparse snpnet model (213 variants) from a pan-trait UKB framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as a common underperforming archetype in external validation. The main limitation is that PGS002046 lacks PRS-only AUC/R² (AUC/R² are null), making performance comparison uncertain; conversely, while PGS001255 reports PRS-only AUROC and R², those come from the sparse pan-trait framework context and include time-to-event phenotyping, which domain guidance treats as a potential endpoint weakness for generic disease-risk use. With only two candidates and incomplete/heterogeneous performance reporting, the best choice is not strongly decisive, hence DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple ovarian cancer / ovarian carcinoma / ovarian neoplasm models). For a broad target of "ovarian neoplasm," the best-supported choice from visible evidence is PGS000082 because it has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: incident ovarian cancer), very large validation (n=211,958), and the best discrimination among broadly comparable ovarian-cancer endpoints in the list (full-model AUROC/C-index ~0.655–0.656) with a disease-focused multi-cohort development context. The main limitation is that reported AUROC/C-index appears to be full-model (covariate-adjusted) rather than PRS-only, and covariates include family history and multiple epidemiologic factors, which domain guidance says should be discounted for inferring standalone PRS quality.

Runners-up: PGS000793 is a near-clone derived from PGS000082 with very similar endpoint and covariates and slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.66), but it is a transformed/inverse-weight variant set, making it less directly supported than the original multi-cohort score given no PRS-only metrics. PGS003385 has very high reported AUROC (0.717) with a directly relevant endpoint (ovarian serous carcinoma, a major ovarian cancer subtype), but it is subtype-specific relative to the umbrella target and the metric comparability remains uncertain (also full-model), so it is kept as a strong but less general runner-up. Exact-label "ovarian neoplasm" PRSweb models (PGS000544–PGS000564) align lexically but show consistently weaker AUROC (~0.52–0.57) and appear to come from a framework/repository setting, so they are not preferred over the stronger, disease-focused multi-cohort ovarian cancer candidates.

All 11 listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (pancreatic carcinoma) via pancreatic cancer / exocrine pancreatic carcinoma, with one clinically dominant subtype model (PGS002264, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma) also plausibly aligned. Best-supported overall is PGS000083 because it has strong endpoint fidelity (incident pancreatic cancer), large European evaluation (n=391,491), and supportive effect-size evidence (HR=1.49, 95% CI 1.36–1.62) alongside consistent full-model discrimination reporting (AUROC 0.745; C-index 0.742). Main limitation: no PRS-only (covariate-isolated) AUROC/R² is provided, and the reported AUROC is from a covariate-adjusted model including family history and smoking/BMI terms, so the metric may be partly covariate-driven and not directly comparable as standalone PRS performance.

Runners-up: (1) PGS000794 is essentially the same 22-variant score family (explicitly derived from PGS000083, inverse weights) with the same endpoint/covariates and nearly identical reported discrimination and HR (AUROC 0.745; HR 1.49), so it remains highly supported but is not clearly superior given it is a transformed variant of the same underlying model family and still lacks PRS-only metrics. (2) PGS000663 has good endpoint fidelity (pancreatic cancer over 0–10 years follow-up), reports a moderate OR per SD (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.25–1.67) and AUROC 0.67, but has a much smaller validation sample (n=956) and includes additional clinical covariates (e.g., diabetic status and anthropometrics), limiting comparability and confidence. PGS002264 reports a very high AUROC (0.83) but is heavily clinically packaged with diabetes status/onset and other clinical risk covariates and has evaluation ancestry not reported, so its apparent performance advantage is discounted for direct PRS selection.

All 11 candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level (trait_efo=Parkinson disease or closely aligned), but several have endpoint shifts (e.g., cognitive/motor progression or Parkinson’s disease dementia) rather than generic PD risk/status. Among the models with phenotyping_reported explicitly as Parkinson’s disease, the strongest visible performance evidence is for PGS000903 (Lancet Neurol 2021; C+T; 1,805 variants), which reports an OR (top 25% vs bottom 25%) of 6.25 (95% CI 4.26–9.28) and an R²=0.054, plus AUROC=0.692 (noted as full-model). This combination provides the most directly PRS-informative metric support in the provided metadata while maintaining clean, basic covariates (PCs, age, sex) and a coherent disease-focused study family.

Runners-up: PGS000902 is from the same Lancet Neurol 2021 meta-analysis family with the same PD endpoint and similarly basic covariates, but it has weaker/less PRS-informative visible metrics (AUROC=0.651; no R²/OR shown). PGS003763 has an incident PD endpoint (still a direct match) with a strong HR (high vs low tertile)=1.72 (1.54–1.93) in a very large validation sample, but it lacks PRS-only/comparable metrics and is time-to-event/incident-focused, making it slightly less aligned to generic PD status than the case-control/status-style PD endpoint models.

Main limitation: across the pool, most AUCs appear to be full-model (not explicitly PGS-only), and covariate sets vary; some high-AUROC candidates (e.g., PGS001774 AUROC=0.8) include multiple non-genetic predictors (family history, head injury, depression, smoking, BMI), which makes the discrimination less comparable to a standalone PRS. This prevents a high-confidence ‘best’ despite PGS000903 having the best visible PRS-comparable evidence.

All four listed models are direct/near-direct matches to the target concept (peripheral vascular disease), but they differ in endpoint fidelity and evidence strength. PGS005217 is best supported because it targets a closely aligned clinical endpoint (incident peripheral artery disease; a key manifestation within the peripheral vascular disease umbrella), comes from a disease-focused PAD study with broad multi-cohort development/validation, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with large variant count (1,296,292), and reports a strong per-SD effect size (HR=1.66) plus a discrimination metric (C-index/full-model 0.731) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). Main limitation: it is PAD-specific (not the broader unspecified PVD label), and the reported C-index is not explicitly PGS-only.

Runners-up: PGS002055 and PGS001843 are exact-label matches to ‘peripheral vascular disease, unspecified’ and share the same portability-framework publication; they provide only weak PRS signal evidence via partial correlation (0.0175 and 0.0151, respectively) and lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2, though PGS002055 is modestly better than PGS001843 on the reported partial-r and uses a genome-wide method with far more variants.
